scores.evidence: Exactly-once effects come from idempotency keys plus unique constraints plus the inbox/outbox pattern. Don't rely on exactly-once delivery.
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate throughout, including subtle areas like month-end anchor clamping, event-time billing, SAQ A scope via hosted fields, and double-entry ledger invariants.

scores.evidence: "Multi-tenant billing" can mean two things... This design covers A and notes where B adds work.
scores.rationale: Explicitly resolves the request's core ambiguity, covers all implied billing capabilities, and is credibly buildable via a phased rollout with explicit deferrals.

scores.evidence: The ledger is the source of truth for balances... Balances are derived from it and can be cached, but they are always rebuildable.
scores.rationale: Components, data ownership and flows connect cleanly; identity, idempotency and immutability choices are applied consistently across every section with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: before a pricing migration, re-rate the last period in shadow mode and diff the invoices
scores.rationale: Test clocks, shadow re-rating and daily reconciliation with alerting target the real risks, but acceptance criteria are mostly unquantified and cross-tenant leak testing is absent.

scores.evidence: The detailed design changes depending on a few things: whether you're in Model A or B, your pricing model... expected scale
scores.rationale: Key sensitivities are named and most figures carry 'e.g.' qualifiers, but targets like 10k events/sec and p99 < 10 ms appear as requirements without being labeled assumptions.

scores.evidence: Kill switches: pause auto-charging globally or per tenant, and pause invoice finalization during an incident.
scores.rationale: Duplicates, late events, out-of-order webhooks, decline handling and reconciliation are concretely handled, but disputes/chargebacks, inbound webhook signature verification and DR/backup are missing or vague.

scores.evidence: SLOs: ingestion durability (no lost events), invoice finalization within N minutes of period end, and entitlement p99 latency.
scores.rationale: Monitoring signals, kill switches and audit logging are concrete, but deployment, rollback, schema migrations and incident ownership are never addressed.

scores.evidence: Billing looks simple and isn't. Proration, tax, dunning, revenue recognition and reconciliation each take serious effort.
scores.rationale: Build-vs-buy weighs engineering cost concretely, but PSP/tax vendor fees, infrastructure cost scaling and any estimates or controls are absent.

scores.evidence: Abstract this behind a tenant→cell routing table from day one.
scores.rationale: The hard-to-reverse choices (tenancy model, price versioning, PSP coupling via adapter, build-vs-buy) are identified and isolated, though exit paths from bought components are not detailed.

scores.evidence: MVP: catalog with versioning, flat/seat subscriptions, PSP integration with webhook inbox, invoices, basic dunning, ledger, entitlements.
scores.rationale: Heavy pieces (Kafka, ClickHouse, cells) are tied to stated volume needs and deferred to later phases, while the MVP is the simplest workable core; buy is recommended where building is unjustified.

scores.evidence: Sharded workers poll with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED WHERE next_action_at <= now()`
scores.rationale: Decisions are specific down to schema sketches and key formats with a dependency-sensible phase order, though phases lack checkable exit criteria and some choices (e.g. Temporal vs. polling) are left open.

checklist.evidence: Money is stored as integer minor units plus an ISO currency code. Never use floats.
Finalized invoices are immutable. Corrections are made with credit notes or a new invoice, never by editing.
Inbox pattern for PSP webhooks: dedupe on event ID and process in order per object, so out-of-order delivery is handled.
collect cards with the PSP's hosted fields or elements and store only tokens
enforced with Postgres Row-Level Security plus a tenant-scoped DB session (`SET app.tenant_id`)
Allow a configurable late-arrival window (e.g. 24–72 hours) before the period is finalized.
Price versions are immutable. Changing a price creates a new version... Grandfathering then works by default.
assign a sequential invoice number (gapless per tenant/legal entity where law requires it)
configurable retry schedule (e.g. days 1, 3, 5, 7). Retry smartly by decline code: never retry hard declines
Reconciliation jobs (daily): ledger vs. PSP balance transactions and payouts... Alert on any non-zero difference.
The product never calls billing synchronously... reads from the Entitlements service, which is fed by subscription events and cached
Build the core (catalog, subscriptions, rating, ledger) and buy the edges (PSP, tax, RevRec)

traps.evidence: Money is stored as integer minor units plus an ISO currency code. Never use floats.
Corrections are made with credit notes or a new invoice, never by editing.
PaymentIntent (idempotency key = invoice_id + attempt_no)... Inbox table (unique on psp_event_id)
PaymentMethod (PSP token only, never raw PAN)
enforced with Postgres Row-Level Security plus a tenant-scoped DB session... also enforce it in the repository layer

note: An unusually precise, internally consistent billing architecture that avoids all classic traps; its main gaps are deployment/rollback operations, dispute and inbound webhook-signature handling, and grounded cost reasoning.
